Abuse.title: Always Worried I Was Not Meant To Be Born
Abuse.body:
Before I was born my parents had gone through two other pregnancies. One of them resulted in my sister, the other tragically ended in a late miscarriage. I was conceived of about a year later and I am nearly certain I was a consolation child for my mother. I do not think my dad wanted me and I think my mom has a deep disappointment over well, me. 



I don't say this without reason. The first thing that comes to mind is that my dad has always hated me and I do mean always. For example my earliest memory of him is a mocking monologue of how I described a television show, the disgust was dripping from his tone. My mom seemed more subtly disgusted by me but it was certainly there. The overcompensated declarations of affection, the perceivable lack of joy in her eyes when around me, and the inverse with my sister all point to that being the case. There's much more I could add but it would be pedantic. I'm confident in how I have judged the situation, but confidence means little when I feel terrible about the whole thing.

  
There's no resentment for how my family feels about me in my heart, but there is a hole where something is missing. The root of that I can only imagine is that the strands of fate simply never intended for it to be filled. Point being I don't think I should have been born nor that I was meant to be born. Perhaps if I was not my consciousness would have ended up somewhere else that was better but who can say. I can say that I wish my parents' other child had been born and that I was not. 



I don't find comfort in thinking my existence is the worse of two options, predictably it fills me with dread. Like there was a cosmic mistake or misdeed when I came to exist as I do now and that it was in some way my fault. Did I take a wrong turn before I could even know it? Should I have died well before now? Would my mom feel better if I did? I don't know, but I suspect those to be true more often than not.

  
I don't want to die, but I do wish I had never existed. I'm not sure I want to change that feeling either so would something like therapy even work?

I'm having my second MA abortion today and I'm so scared about the pain. I've been reading how women say its the most painful thing they've gone through and I'm having anxiety attacks and I'm so scared I won't cope with it.

My first was 3 months after I'd given birth in 2022 and honestly was completely manageable. From what I remember it was strong period type cramps that only lasted about 2 hours and the whole process was over in around 4-6 hours. I'd taken the 4 pills vaginally, started bleeding after about 2 hours, with mild cramping and bloating. Pain reached maybe a 6 and lots of clotting and then after it eased right up. Could definitely manage that again. I was 8 weeks 1 day at the time of termination

Is the pain the second time likely going to be the same as the first? How long roughly is there severe pain for people that experience it and what do you do in terms of pain management? Last time I was given codeine but this time they refused and told me to buy co-codamol over the counter. 

I'm absolutely terrified right now.

Medical.title: Super sure before my abortion and now feel horrible
Medical.body:
Hey everyone, throwaway account for obvious reasons.
I had a surgical abortion 6 days ago, I was 9 weeks pregnant.
I’m almost 32 and have been with my boyfriend for 1.5 years. 
When I found out I was pregnant I immediately knew I wanted an abortion, there were no warm feelings towards the fetus, I was very annoyed how it was changing and messing with my body already,  my boobs went a cup bigger and the nausea was incapacitating. 
Aside from the physical symptoms I am not really ready to have a child right now, I’ve been out of work for 8 months and am only starting a new job next month, my boyfriend and I don’t really live in the same city, he currently doesn’t even have a permanent home of his own because he recently finished his camper van and has been bouncing between my city, the Canary Islands, his hometown and the city he last lived permanently. I think partly because of this back and forth our relationship has had its rocky patches.
We had also talked about it before and both agreed that we’re not ready yet to have kids. I wasn’t even sure I ever wanted kids.

So it was a super easy decision and one we didn’t hesitate to make. In the two weeks leading up to the appointment I was super sure and very calm and went about my life as normally as I could, I went to a festival (took some psychedelics), to a wedding and tried not to let the pregnancy bother me.

Fast forward to the day of the abortion, I went in very calm and collected, was even confused why the clinic staff treated me so kindly and carefully. The doctor even held my hand until I was out from the anaesthetic.

When I woke up I had my first crying spell. My boyfriend picked me up and the first couple of days I was mostly fine aside from the bleeding.

Then everything shifted and I have been going through intense grief, heavy crying spells and anxiety.
I’m worried I made a mistake, that I do truly want a family and that this was my only chance because I’m so old already. I’m also worried my boyfriend will never be ready and I will be left waiting until it’s too late. 
There’s many more intrusive thoughts around those topics but mostly I’m just so so sad.

Has anyone experienced this? And does it pass? Rationally speaking I know that all my reasons for having the abortion were and are still valid, and that there is still plenty of time to have a child, but emotionally I wish I could go back, so I would still have a choice. I don’t know if my decision would end up being different but I feel so awful right now. I want this to stop :(

Edit to add: I’m just so confused because I was so sure and calm and I don’t understand why this is so hard on me right now.

Hey everyone, throwaway account for obvious reasons.
I had a surgical abortion 6 days ago, I was 9 weeks pregnant.

When I found out I was pregnant I immediately knew I wanted an abortion, there were no warm feelings towards the fetus, I was very annoyed how it was changing and messing with my body already,  my boobs went a cup bigger and the nausea was incapacitating.

Discrimination.title: Why does society expectations about having one of each genders mess with us?
Discrimination.body:
I know there are people out there who say they generally don’t care what genders their babies are. I wish I was one of those people. First and foremost, of course I just want happy and healthy children and I know whatever I get I will love them! Yes, we all know that there are people out there who struggle with conceiving or who have a bad experience in having children. I get that! 
We have had a miscarriage in between having our children and it was a hard experience to go through. I feel society constantly makes you feel like having one of each is the ultimate dream. We are always reminded by these expectations! I know I cannot control the gender, but I just wish I didn’t feel I wasn’t missing out on not having a daughter. When I think deeply about why I want a daughter, it’s basically because I get caught up worrying about what other people say about our family or them placing their pity over us for having only boys. I hate the feeling! I love my boys, but wish I had the experience of parenting both genders as well as having my boys. I would not have another one just to try for a girl. I would only have another knowing I am 100% content about having another boy. I feel when my parents or in laws talk about it you can sense their disappointment and it makes me feel sad. Anyone else know what I mean? Can you connect to this post? If so, talk me through how you feel now and how you overcame these annoying feelings.

Abuse.title: Always Worried I Was Not Meant To Be Born
Abuse.body:
Before I was born my parents had gone through two other pregnancies. One of them resulted in my sister, the other tragically ended in a late miscarriage. I was conceived of about a year later and I am nearly certain I was a consolation child for my mother. I do not think my dad wanted me and I think my mom has a deep disappointment over well, me. 



I don't say this without reason. The first thing that comes to mind is that my dad has always hated me and I do mean always. For example my earliest memory of him is a mocking monologue of how I described a television show, the disgust was dripping from his tone. My mom seemed more subtly disgusted by me but it was certainly there. The overcompensated declarations of affection, the perceivable lack of joy in her eyes when around me, and the inverse with my sister all point to that being the case. There's much more I could add but it would be pedantic. I'm confident in how I have judged the situation, but confidence means little when I feel terrible about the whole thing.

  
There's no resentment for how my family feels about me in my heart, but there is a hole where something is missing. The root of that I can only imagine is that the strands of fate simply never intended for it to be filled. Point being I don't think I should have been born nor that I was meant to be born. Perhaps if I was not my consciousness would have ended up somewhere else that was better but who can say. I can say that I wish my parents' other child had been born and that I was not. 



I don't find comfort in thinking my existence is the worse of two options, predictably it fills me with dread. Like there was a cosmic mistake or misdeed when I came to exist as I do now and that it was in some way my fault. Did I take a wrong turn before I could even know it? Should I have died well before now? Would my mom feel better if I did? I don't know, but I suspect those to be true more often than not.

  
I don't want to die, but I do wish I had never existed. I'm not sure I want to change that feeling either so would something like therapy even work?

Aggression.title: Legal Action Advice
Aggression.body:
About three/four weeks ago I went through an incident of sexual harassment/assault at work from a customer. He was black out drunk (I work at a pub) and the way it was handled by my work wasn’t very professional. He was kicked out and told he wasn’t allowed to come back in to pay his tab without talking to my boss or my male coworker first since I made it clear I did not want to have contact with him. 

Well my boss allowed him to come into work yesterday without informing me. And not just to pay his tab, he was allowed to stay and drink. Thankfully I had someone else covering the opening part of my shift but was planning on coming in earlier to help with the bar since there was an event so I knew the restaurant was super busy. I was notified by my male coworker that he showed up so I had to wait till he was gone to come in for my shift. 

One of my regulars is a state trooper and he pulled me aside to tell me that from a professional view, I could take it further if the incident made me this uncomfortable (he wasn’t informed much on what happened). I didn’t have intent to pursue anything legal cause I thought he’d be barred on the days i work, but now I’m not sure what I want to do. 

The statie told me that the guy admits he doesn’t remember what happened but takes full accountability for it and that he wants to apologize to me in person but on my terms. My boss also has talked about him coming in to apologize and I’ve expressed very clearly before that I don’t want to talk to him or hear an “I’m sorry for sexually assaulting you” apology, even if he has owned up to what happened. 

I just wanted to not have him in when I’m working or still be there when I’m into work. He’s been very drunk/overserved numerous times before this incident, and now dealing with that, i don’t want to deal with what could happen if he got blacked out drunk again (if he didn’t remember what he did, he could just as well do it again). But now since he’s just allowed back I’m not sure what legal action I could take if i chose to do that. What would be the options I could take? Cause honestly my biggest option is just quitting my job and working at a different place since it’s not the first sexual harassment incident I’ve gone through and it’s definitely not the last, and it’s clear my boss can’t handle dealing with situations properly.

Medical.title: Super sure before my abortion and now feel horrible
Medical.body:
Hey everyone, throwaway account for obvious reasons.
I had a surgical abortion 6 days ago, I was 9 weeks pregnant.
I’m almost 32 and have been with my boyfriend for 1.5 years. 
When I found out I was pregnant I immediately knew I wanted an abortion, there were no warm feelings towards the fetus, I was very annoyed how it was changing and messing with my body already,  my boobs went a cup bigger and the nausea was incapacitating. 
Aside from the physical symptoms I am not really ready to have a child right now, I’ve been out of work for 8 months and am only starting a new job next month, my boyfriend and I don’t really live in the same city, he currently doesn’t even have a permanent home of his own because he recently finished his camper van and has been bouncing between my city, the Canary Islands, his hometown and the city he last lived permanently. I think partly because of this back and forth our relationship has had its rocky patches.
We had also talked about it before and both agreed that we’re not ready yet to have kids. I wasn’t even sure I ever wanted kids.

So it was a super easy decision and one we didn’t hesitate to make. In the two weeks leading up to the appointment I was super sure and very calm and went about my life as normally as I could, I went to a festival (took some psychedelics), to a wedding and tried not to let the pregnancy bother me.

Fast forward to the day of the abortion, I went in very calm and collected, was even confused why the clinic staff treated me so kindly and carefully. The doctor even held my hand until I was out from the anaesthetic.

When I woke up I had my first crying spell. My boyfriend picked me up and the first couple of days I was mostly fine aside from the bleeding.

Then everything shifted and I have been going through intense grief, heavy crying spells and anxiety.
I’m worried I made a mistake, that I do truly want a family and that this was my only chance because I’m so old already. I’m also worried my boyfriend will never be ready and I will be left waiting until it’s too late. 
There’s many more intrusive thoughts around those topics but mostly I’m just so so sad.

Has anyone experienced this? And does it pass? Rationally speaking I know that all my reasons for having the abortion were and are still valid, and that there is still plenty of time to have a child, but emotionally I wish I could go back, so I would still have a choice. I don’t know if my decision would end up being different but I feel so awful right now. I want this to stop :(

Edit to add: I’m just so confused because I was so sure and calm and I don’t understand why this is so hard on me right now.

I'm having my second MA abortion today and I'm so scared about the pain. I've been reading how women say its the most painful thing they've gone through and I'm having anxiety attacks and I'm so scared I won't cope with it.

My first was 3 months after I'd given birth in 2022 and honestly was completely manageable. From what I remember it was strong period type cramps that only lasted about 2 hours and the whole process was over in around 4-6 hours. I'd taken the 4 pills vaginally, started bleeding after about 2 hours, with mild cramping and bloating. Pain reached maybe a 6 and lots of clotting and then after it eased right up. Could definitely manage that again. I was 8 weeks 1 day at the time of termination

Is the pain the second time likely going to be the same as the first? How long roughly is there severe pain for people that experience it and what do you do in terms of pain management? Last time I was given codeine but this time they refused and told me to buy co-codamol over the counter. 

I'm absolutely terrified right now.

Discrimination.title: Why does society expectations about having one of each genders mess with us?
Discrimination.body:
I know there are people out there who say they generally don’t care what genders their babies are. I wish I was one of those people. First and foremost, of course I just want happy and healthy children and I know whatever I get I will love them! Yes, we all know that there are people out there who struggle with conceiving or who have a bad experience in having children. I get that! 
We have had a miscarriage in between having our children and it was a hard experience to go through. I feel society constantly makes you feel like having one of each is the ultimate dream. We are always reminded by these expectations! I know I cannot control the gender, but I just wish I didn’t feel I wasn’t missing out on not having a daughter. When I think deeply about why I want a daughter, it’s basically because I get caught up worrying about what other people say about our family or them placing their pity over us for having only boys. I hate the feeling! I love my boys, but wish I had the experience of parenting both genders as well as having my boys. I would not have another one just to try for a girl. I would only have another knowing I am 100% content about having another boy. I feel when my parents or in laws talk about it you can sense their disappointment and it makes me feel sad. Anyone else know what I mean? Can you connect to this post? If so, talk me through how you feel now and how you overcame these annoying feelings.

Pregnancy.title: Super sure before my abortion and now feel horrible
Pregnancy.body:
Hey everyone, throwaway account for obvious reasons.
I had a surgical abortion 6 days ago, I was 9 weeks pregnant.
I’m almost 32 and have been with my boyfriend for 1.5 years. 
When I found out I was pregnant I immediately knew I wanted an abortion, there were no warm feelings towards the fetus, I was very annoyed how it was changing and messing with my body already,  my boobs went a cup bigger and the nausea was incapacitating. 
Aside from the physical symptoms I am not really ready to have a child right now, I’ve been out of work for 8 months and am only starting a new job next month, my boyfriend and I don’t really live in the same city, he currently doesn’t even have a permanent home of his own because he recently finished his camper van and has been bouncing between my city, the Canary Islands, his hometown and the city he last lived permanently. I think partly because of this back and forth our relationship has had its rocky patches.
We had also talked about it before and both agreed that we’re not ready yet to have kids. I wasn’t even sure I ever wanted kids.

So it was a super easy decision and one we didn’t hesitate to make. In the two weeks leading up to the appointment I was super sure and very calm and went about my life as normally as I could, I went to a festival (took some psychedelics), to a wedding and tried not to let the pregnancy bother me.

Fast forward to the day of the abortion, I went in very calm and collected, was even confused why the clinic staff treated me so kindly and carefully. The doctor even held my hand until I was out from the anaesthetic.

When I woke up I had my first crying spell. My boyfriend picked me up and the first couple of days I was mostly fine aside from the bleeding.

Then everything shifted and I have been going through intense grief, heavy crying spells and anxiety.
I’m worried I made a mistake, that I do truly want a family and that this was my only chance because I’m so old already. I’m also worried my boyfriend will never be ready and I will be left waiting until it’s too late. 
There’s many more intrusive thoughts around those topics but mostly I’m just so so sad.

Has anyone experienced this? And does it pass? Rationally speaking I know that all my reasons for having the abortion were and are still valid, and that there is still plenty of time to have a child, but emotionally I wish I could go back, so I would still have a choice. I don’t know if my decision would end up being different but I feel so awful right now. I want this to stop :(

Edit to add: I’m just so confused because I was so sure and calm and I don’t understand why this is so hard on me right now.

Medical.title: Haven’t Had a Period Since My Suction Abortion – Was the June 3 Spotting My Period?
Medical.body:
Hi everyone,

I had a suction abortion (manual vacuum aspiration) on **April 19th, 2025**. I was just **1 month and 1 week pregnant** at the time. I’m now over 9 weeks post-procedure, and I still haven’t had a full period, so I’m hoping to get some thoughts or shared experiences.

Here’s what’s happened:

* **Post-abortion:** I recovered normally with no pain or heavy bleeding.
* On **May 21–22,** I had intense lower abdominal cramps, but they went away after two days.
* On **June 3**, I saw some red blood on the tissue paper while wiping after urinating. It looked like a small amount of fresh blood — similar to what I might see on day 3–4 of a typical period — but it only lasted half a day. I wore a pad, but there was no blood on it at all. Little cramps but no breast tenderness or PMS-like symptoms.
* On **June 19**, I had another episode of strong cramping and pulsating pain in the lower abdomen, along with intense pain in the pelvic region during bowel movements. I went to the clinic the next day, where they performed all the necessary tests and an ultrasound, and said everything looked normal.

As of today (**June 24**), I still haven’t had a proper period. I’m not on any birth control, and I don’t have a history of irregular periods or PCOS. I do have subclinical hypothyroidism, and I tested positive for **thyroid peroxidase antibodies** earlier this year **(TPO 60)**, but my thyroid levels were said to be in the normal range recently **(TSH 2.35).**

My main questions are:

* Was the June 3rd spotting likely my first period, or just hormonal spotting?
* Is it normal to still not have a period more than 9 weeks after a suction abortion?

Would really appreciate any insight, especially from people who had delayed periods after surgical abortion. Thanks so much.

If anyone has been through something like this or has experience with later abortion, I’d really appreciate any advice, support, or just to hear that I’m not alone.

Thank you for reading.

Pregnancy.title: Haven’t Had a Period Since My Suction Abortion – Was the June 3 Spotting My Period?
Pregnancy.body:
Hi everyone,

I had a suction abortion (manual vacuum aspiration) on **April 19th, 2025**. I was just **1 month and 1 week pregnant** at the time. I’m now over 9 weeks post-procedure, and I still haven’t had a full period, so I’m hoping to get some thoughts or shared experiences.

Here’s what’s happened:

* **Post-abortion:** I recovered normally with no pain or heavy bleeding.
* On **May 21–22,** I had intense lower abdominal cramps, but they went away after two days.
* On **June 3**, I saw some red blood on the tissue paper while wiping after urinating. It looked like a small amount of fresh blood — similar to what I might see on day 3–4 of a typical period — but it only lasted half a day. I wore a pad, but there was no blood on it at all. Little cramps but no breast tenderness or PMS-like symptoms.
* On **June 19**, I had another episode of strong cramping and pulsating pain in the lower abdomen, along with intense pain in the pelvic region during bowel movements. I went to the clinic the next day, where they performed all the necessary tests and an ultrasound, and said everything looked normal.

As of today (**June 24**), I still haven’t had a proper period. I’m not on any birth control, and I don’t have a history of irregular periods or PCOS. I do have subclinical hypothyroidism, and I tested positive for **thyroid peroxidase antibodies** earlier this year **(TPO 60)**, but my thyroid levels were said to be in the normal range recently **(TSH 2.35).**

My main questions are:

* Was the June 3rd spotting likely my first period, or just hormonal spotting?
* Is it normal to still not have a period more than 9 weeks after a suction abortion?

Would really appreciate any insight, especially from people who had delayed periods after surgical abortion. Thanks so much.

Abuse.title: Always Worried I Was Not Meant To Be Born
Abuse.body:
Before I was born my parents had gone through two other pregnancies. One of them resulted in my sister, the other tragically ended in a late miscarriage. I was conceived of about a year later and I am nearly certain I was a consolation child for my mother. I do not think my dad wanted me and I think my mom has a deep disappointment over well, me. 



I don't say this without reason. The first thing that comes to mind is that my dad has always hated me and I do mean always. For example my earliest memory of him is a mocking monologue of how I described a television show, the disgust was dripping from his tone. My mom seemed more subtly disgusted by me but it was certainly there. The overcompensated declarations of affection, the perceivable lack of joy in her eyes when around me, and the inverse with my sister all point to that being the case. There's much more I could add but it would be pedantic. I'm confident in how I have judged the situation, but confidence means little when I feel terrible about the whole thing.

  
There's no resentment for how my family feels about me in my heart, but there is a hole where something is missing. The root of that I can only imagine is that the strands of fate simply never intended for it to be filled. Point being I don't think I should have been born nor that I was meant to be born. Perhaps if I was not my consciousness would have ended up somewhere else that was better but who can say. I can say that I wish my parents' other child had been born and that I was not. 



I don't find comfort in thinking my existence is the worse of two options, predictably it fills me with dread. Like there was a cosmic mistake or misdeed when I came to exist as I do now and that it was in some way my fault. Did I take a wrong turn before I could even know it? Should I have died well before now? Would my mom feel better if I did? I don't know, but I suspect those to be true more often than not.

  
I don't want to die, but I do wish I had never existed. I'm not sure I want to change that feeling either so would something like therapy even work?

Abuse.title: Will I ever be able to build a real bond and life with my daughter?
Abuse.body:
So, as the title states, I’m (21m) at a serious loss here and am looking for some sound advice, reassurance, something. My first-born, my beautiful daughter, just turned 7 months old yesterday, on the 22nd. Due to her mother’s (20f) irresponsibility and childish behavior, I’ve missed out on basically everything thus far that has to do with my baby.

Both of us had rough childhoods and we met in juvie (red flag #1) about 8 years ago. We were on and off for basically the whole time, with her being the only woman I talked to or considered a relationship with at the time, as I had so much going on, and her running around. I got sent to prison for 2 years when I was 16, and we had a miscarriage right before I went in. I’m not gonna go into detail, but she had a child shortly after I got out, while she was a minor, with a grown man more than 6 years her senior. 

Eventually, I moved back home from out of state and started talking to her while she had a boyfriend, because she told me they broke up. I was actually on probation in another state and got it transferred so I could come back home and have a relationship with her. Her and her ex split up, and I found out from her that he was apparently sterile, which will be relevant later. She moved in with me, we got engaged and had plans to get married, and all went well for ~3 months until we split up and she went back to her ex.

Two weeks later, she texts me and tells me she’s pregnant. Obviously, with her ex being sterile, I was the only one who could’ve been the father, and the dates for her last period, estimated conception date, and due date all lined up with me, and made it impossible for it to be his, not even mentioning the fact that he is sterile, which one of his ex-friends even showed me texts he sent with the medical documentation, so we knew this whole time that it was my child.

She swore up and down that the child was mine, and that she’d let me be involved, and then she did a baby shower and gender reveal  with her boyfriend and posted it on all her social media pages pretending that he was the father, and didn’t even tell me she had found out the gender prior. Shortly after this, she blocked me on everything, and the only updates I got were from our mutual friends, who were checking her pages to see if my child was born, until November, when she WAS born.

During this time, ofc I had to move on, sometimes it just clicks and you know you’ve got the one. I got married pretty quickly to the woman I’ve searched for my whole life, and my wife and I are expecting another baby in December. I filed court cases myself, and I went through the Office of the Attorney General to try to get them to investigate using child support as a basis, before they told me that I’d have to handle it on my own as they could not get in contact with the mother to obtain vital information they needed, even though I gave them her, her bf, and her families names, numbers, emails, and addresses.

Eventually, her and her ex broke up because he did a DNA test about 3 months ago and he had solid evidence it wasn’t his, so him and his family kicked her and her two kids out. Since then, she’s been living with her Mom and, once I found out, I messaged her offering to help as long as she let me be in my babies life, and she’s let me be involved since.

Here’s the problem though: I’ve missed so much in my daughter’s life, I feel like I’m a stranger and I don’t know her. I wasn’t allowed there for the birth or when she was a newborn. She went through the most important skin-to -skin phases as an infant with a stranger she’s never gonna meet pretending he’s her father. She didn’t hear my voice in the womb, so she doesn’t know my voice or my face. Shes gonna have to get a helmet cause she has a flat head from not getting enough tummy time as a newborn, so I feel like such a failure because I wasn’t able to keep her safe. She’s a very happy baby, so I can make her smile, but she cries so much, and she won’t let me hold her like a baby:(

My mother chose drugs over me when I was an infant, and my father worked and shut himself in my room as a child, so was basically absent. How can I give my daughter a better life than I had, a better father than I had, when she doesn’t hardly know me? How can I bond with her when I missed the moments that were supposed to cement her Daddy in her brain? I’m scared that she’s gonna think I love the new baby more or her less when she gets older because of what I missed.

TLDR; BM kept me out of my babies life, now my baby doesn’t hardly know me and I don’t know how to be a good father for her

Abuse.body:
So, like the title said I very unfortunately found out about a month and a half ago my husband [28m] cheated on me. I know for a fact about 3 times, but I have to assume there was more. It was all with the same woman, I think she's 31 or 32 & they work together. She was a guest at our wedding 🫠

He cheated on me while I was doing IVF.. I had 3 miscarriages 1 before and 2 right after we were married. And my point in including that is i literally cried and cried to my best friend, she encouraged me to keep going and have faith. And aside from the fact she saw how much I was struggling, and crying to her because I knew how badly he wanted to be a dad.. I'm really hurt she was going to let me get pregnant knowing I was being cheated on.

Her husband also knew, he's pretty good friends with mine.

She also comforted me right after I found out, at that point I only knew about one occasion because I walked into it. 

I found out recently she knew about him cheating before our wedding... she found out the very first time he did it, let me marry him. Was my maid of honour 

If you're wondering, the way I found out was my (ex) husband came to our house. He moved out, but came back to apologize and promised to tell me everything and gave me his phone for proof. He told me who all knew, two of his friends and her. 

I saw texts between them.

There was a very odd conversation that made my stomach turn where he texted her saying he needed someone to talk to, because he "f*cked up again" and she was oddly sympathetic towards him


I will say, she was defending me to an extent in the rest of the conversations and arguing with him. But regardless, I wouldn't let her marry someone or have babies with them if I knew about cheating.

I'll never forgive him, but I'm really trying to see this from her perspective. I'm hurt, but we have been friends for 14 years... she said she wanted me to be happy and she thought he was changing. She also told me we should try couples therapy.. despite the fact I have said I'm done. 

There was literally never one sign from her, she never voiced any concern about our relationship and anytime I talked about him she went on about how much he loved me, how lucky I was etc. 

Also, we were raised religious. All of us, and she keeps guilting me that divorce is not okay.. yet wants me to forgive cheating?

Aggression.title: What should I do if I'm being stalked for almost four years now?
Aggression.body: Here's how it started - I was new to facebook, and I made my phone number public by mistake. Now this guy calls me up, informs me that my phone number was public. We had this one person in our mutuals who was a nice guy(we went to the same school) who didn't have random unknown people on his friendlist. So I assumed he was not a bad person, so I had a few small chit chats with him. Valentine's day was like just around the corner and I was fucking 15 at that time and the only thing that grabbed my attention was Powerpuff girls and he was talking about love and shi. I freaked out obviously. I made it clear that I am just 15 and I was clearly not into him. He kept on insisting so I had to block him. Now he has been calling me every months from 4-7 new phone numbers and I have to block all of them. I'm turning 18 this january (2022). I live in India, and if you aren't aware then imma tell you this- rape cases, molestation, harassment, acid attacks are extremely frequent here. He has found a lot about me and it is honestly scary. I told my parents about this, but I have my entrance exams going on so I don't really go out of my house right now. This one time my maa picked up his call because truecaller showed the location of Bihar(the stalker lives there too, like that is his hometown. I can tell by his surname, and the number of times I've got calls from Bihar. But he lives in my city so he probably goes there occasionally.) Aggression.title: Legal Action Advice
Aggression.body:
About three/four weeks ago I went through an incident of sexual harassment/assault at work from a customer. He was black out drunk (I work at a pub) and the way it was handled by my work wasn’t very professional. He was kicked out and told he wasn’t allowed to come back in to pay his tab without talking to my boss or my male coworker first since I made it clear I did not want to have contact with him. 

Well my boss allowed him to come into work yesterday without informing me. And not just to pay his tab, he was allowed to stay and drink. Thankfully I had someone else covering the opening part of my shift but was planning on coming in earlier to help with the bar since there was an event so I knew the restaurant was super busy. I was notified by my male coworker that he showed up so I had to wait till he was gone to come in for my shift. 

One of my regulars is a state trooper and he pulled me aside to tell me that from a professional view, I could take it further if the incident made me this uncomfortable (he wasn’t informed much on what happened). I didn’t have intent to pursue anything legal cause I thought he’d be barred on the days i work, but now I’m not sure what I want to do. 

The statie told me that the guy admits he doesn’t remember what happened but takes full accountability for it and that he wants to apologize to me in person but on my terms. My boss also has talked about him coming in to apologize and I’ve expressed very clearly before that I don’t want to talk to him or hear an “I’m sorry for sexually assaulting you” apology, even if he has owned up to what happened. 

I just wanted to not have him in when I’m working or still be there when I’m into work. He’s been very drunk/overserved numerous times before this incident, and now dealing with that, i don’t want to deal with what could happen if he got blacked out drunk again (if he didn’t remember what he did, he could just as well do it again). But now since he’s just allowed back I’m not sure what legal action I could take if i chose to do that. What would be the options I could take? Cause honestly my biggest option is just quitting my job and working at a different place since it’s not the first sexual harassment incident I’ve gone through and it’s definitely not the last, and it’s clear my boss can’t handle dealing with situations properly.

Medical.title: Super sure before my abortion and now feel horrible
Medical.body:
Hey everyone, throwaway account for obvious reasons.
I had a surgical abortion 6 days ago, I was 9 weeks pregnant.
I’m almost 32 and have been with my boyfriend for 1.5 years. 
When I found out I was pregnant I immediately knew I wanted an abortion, there were no warm feelings towards the fetus, I was very annoyed how it was changing and messing with my body already,  my boobs went a cup bigger and the nausea was incapacitating. 
Aside from the physical symptoms I am not really ready to have a child right now, I’ve been out of work for 8 months and am only starting a new job next month, my boyfriend and I don’t really live in the same city, he currently doesn’t even have a permanent home of his own because he recently finished his camper van and has been bouncing between my city, the Canary Islands, his hometown and the city he last lived permanently. I think partly because of this back and forth our relationship has had its rocky patches.
We had also talked about it before and both agreed that we’re not ready yet to have kids. I wasn’t even sure I ever wanted kids.

So it was a super easy decision and one we didn’t hesitate to make. In the two weeks leading up to the appointment I was super sure and very calm and went about my life as normally as I could, I went to a festival (took some psychedelics), to a wedding and tried not to let the pregnancy bother me.

Fast forward to the day of the abortion, I went in very calm and collected, was even confused why the clinic staff treated me so kindly and carefully. The doctor even held my hand until I was out from the anaesthetic.

When I woke up I had my first crying spell. My boyfriend picked me up and the first couple of days I was mostly fine aside from the bleeding.

Then everything shifted and I have been going through intense grief, heavy crying spells and anxiety.
I’m worried I made a mistake, that I do truly want a family and that this was my only chance because I’m so old already. I’m also worried my boyfriend will never be ready and I will be left waiting until it’s too late. 
There’s many more intrusive thoughts around those topics but mostly I’m just so so sad.

Has anyone experienced this? And does it pass? Rationally speaking I know that all my reasons for having the abortion were and are still valid, and that there is still plenty of time to have a child, but emotionally I wish I could go back, so I would still have a choice. I don’t know if my decision would end up being different but I feel so awful right now. I want this to stop :(

Edit to add: I’m just so confused because I was so sure and calm and I don’t understand why this is so hard on me right now.

Medical.title: Struggling to feel excited in first trimester
Medical.body:
TW: talk of infant death and miscarriage. 

I (f21) am expecting my first baby with my husband (m23). I really want to be happy and excited and hopeful, but ever since I was a little girl and I found out about miscarriage/stillbirth, I’ve had such a deep fear of pregnancy/child loss. 

Lmp date was 4/20/2025, but at our first ultrasound when I should have been almost 9 weeks, baby was measuring at 6w 5d and they found a large (more than 50% the size of the sac) SCH adjacent to the gestational sac. There was no real reason or explanation for either thing and I feel like I was sent home to either miscarry or not until our next appointment on July 17th where I should be 10.5 weeks. Our fetus is confirmed IUP and viable with a good heartbeat. 

I know I should try to hold on to the indescribable joy of hearing our child’s heartbeat for the first time, but seeing the massive pocket of blood directly afterwards and being told we are measuring 2.5 weeks behind has unfortunately overshadowed that beautiful moment and made me feel like I can’t be happy or excited. 

With the lack of information of course fell into a Google search hole and from what I can tell, my risk of pregnancy loss or stillbirth has gone up quite significantly. Everytime the nausea eases up or my boobs feel slightly less sore I’m horrified that my baby is just dead. 

I just don’t know how to be happy or excited when the risk of loss is so great. I keep trying to remind myself that I am pregnant today and that’s all that matters. I’ve greatly increased my vitamin c, d and A Lipaic acid intake within my diet to help the sch heal and reabsorb and so far at 8w 2d I have not had any bleeding or spotting. I’m resting as much as I can and I’ve put myself on pelvic rest to try to help my body and hopefully not bleed. 

Idk. I just feel like I’m doing all I can but I can’t help but feel soooo guilty for how negative I’m feeling. My family keeps saying to just manifest good things and put good vibes out there, so I can’t help but feel like if I do lose the baby it’ll be because of my inability to be happy and hopeful all the time. 

Through all of this, my husband has been my absolute rock and safe space. He has lit up this experience so much and kept me as positive and happy as possible, but he’s on a work trip this week and I’m just here alone with the dogs trying to take care of all of us all while scrutinizing every tiny change in cramping and discharge and just waiting for something awful to happen. I just really don’t want to miscarry while he’s away. I really don’t want to miscarry at all. I understand that in the human experience it is a negative thing to wish to a positive experience, and a positive thing to embrace a negative experience, but how the fuck do I embrace this awful feeling. I feel like I’ll never be able to breathe again, even if the baby ends up being born how am I going to deal with the anxiety of SIDS or car accidents or fucking lightning striking my child. How do moms do this??

Mental Health.title: I’m 20 weeks pregnant and
Mental Health.body:
Hi everyone,

I just recently found out that I’m 20 weeks pregnant. I have very irregular periods, so I genuinely had no idea I was pregnant until about a week ago when I started feeling nauseous and went to get checked. It was a complete shock.

I’m in Minnesota, and I’m trying to figure out what my options for abortion are at this stage. I already have a child who is autistic, and I’m doing everything I can to give them the love, time, and support they need. I just don’t feel like I’m in the right place mentally, emotionally, or financially to bring another child into the world right now. I feel overwhelmed and scared, and honestly… guilty for even thinking about abortion this far along.

I keep wondering if I’m a horrible person for not wanting to go through with this pregnancy, but deep down I know I’m trying to make the best decision for everyone involved including the child I already have.

If anyone has been through something like this or has experience with later abortion, I’d really appreciate any advice, support, or just to hear that I’m not alone.

Thank you for reading.

Discrimination.title: Why does society expectations about having one of each genders mess with us?
Discrimination.body:
I know there are people out there who say they generally don’t care what genders their babies are. I wish I was one of those people. First and foremost, of course I just want happy and healthy children and I know whatever I get I will love them! Yes, we all know that there are people out there who struggle with conceiving or who have a bad experience in having children. I get that! 
We have had a miscarriage in between having our children and it was a hard experience to go through. I feel society constantly makes you feel like having one of each is the ultimate dream. We are always reminded by these expectations! I know I cannot control the gender, but I just wish I didn’t feel I wasn’t missing out on not having a daughter. When I think deeply about why I want a daughter, it’s basically because I get caught up worrying about what other people say about our family or them placing their pity over us for having only boys. I hate the feeling! I love my boys, but wish I had the experience of parenting both genders as well as having my boys. I would not have another one just to try for a girl. I would only have another knowing I am 100% content about having another boy. I feel when my parents or in laws talk about it you can sense their disappointment and it makes me feel sad. Anyone else know what I mean? Can you connect to this post? If so, talk me through how you feel now and how you overcame these annoying feelings.

Aside from the physical symptoms I am not really ready to have a child right now, I’ve been out of work for 8 months and am only starting a new job next month, my boyfriend and I don’t really live in the same city, he currently doesn’t even have a permanent home of his own because he recently finished his camper van and has been bouncing between my city, the Canary Islands, his hometown and the city he last lived permanently. I think partly because of this back and forth our relationship has had its rocky patches.
We had also talked about it before and both agreed that we’re not ready yet to have kids. I wasn’t even sure I ever wanted kids.

So it was a super easy decision and one we didn’t hesitate to make. In the two weeks leading up to the appointment I was super sure and very calm and went about my life as normally as I could, I went to a festival (took some psychedelics), to a wedding and tried not to let the pregnancy bother me.

When I woke up I had my first crying spell. My boyfriend picked me up and the first couple of days I was mostly fine aside from the bleeding.

Then everything shifted and I have been going through intense grief, heavy crying spells and anxiety.
I’m worried I made a mistake, that I do truly want a family and that this was my only chance because I’m so old already. I’m also worried my boyfriend will never be ready and I will be left waiting until it’s too late. 
There’s many more intrusive thoughts around those topics but mostly I’m just so so sad.

Has anyone experienced this? And does it pass? Rationally speaking I know that all my reasons for having the abortion were and are still valid, and that there is still plenty of time to have a child, but emotionally I wish I could go back, so I would still have a choice. I don’t know if my decision would end up being different but I feel so awful right now. I want this to stop :(

Pregnancy.title: I’m 20 weeks pregnant and
Pregnancy.body:
Hi everyone,

I just recently found out that I’m 20 weeks pregnant. I have very irregular periods, so I genuinely had no idea I was pregnant until about a week ago when I started feeling nauseous and went to get checked. It was a complete shock.

I’m in Minnesota, and I’m trying to figure out what my options for abortion are at this stage. I already have a child who is autistic, and I’m doing everything I can to give them the love, time, and support they need. I just don’t feel like I’m in the right place mentally, emotionally, or financially to bring another child into the world right now. I feel overwhelmed and scared, and honestly… guilty for even thinking about abortion this far along.

I keep wondering if I’m a horrible person for not wanting to go through with this pregnancy, but deep down I know I’m trying to make the best decision for everyone involved including the child I already have.

If anyone has been through something like this or has experience with later abortion, I’d really appreciate any advice, support, or just to hear that I’m not alone.

Thank you for reading.

Abuse.title: Always Worried I Was Not Meant To Be Born
Abuse.body:
Before I was born my parents had gone through two other pregnancies. One of them resulted in my sister, the other tragically ended in a late miscarriage. I was conceived of about a year later and I am nearly certain I was a consolation child for my mother. I do not think my dad wanted me and I think my mom has a deep disappointment over well, me. 



I don't say this without reason. The first thing that comes to mind is that my dad has always hated me and I do mean always. For example my earliest memory of him is a mocking monologue of how I described a television show, the disgust was dripping from his tone. My mom seemed more subtly disgusted by me but it was certainly there. The overcompensated declarations of affection, the perceivable lack of joy in her eyes when around me, and the inverse with my sister all point to that being the case. There's much more I could add but it would be pedantic. I'm confident in how I have judged the situation, but confidence means little when I feel terrible about the whole thing.

  
There's no resentment for how my family feels about me in my heart, but there is a hole where something is missing. The root of that I can only imagine is that the strands of fate simply never intended for it to be filled. Point being I don't think I should have been born nor that I was meant to be born. Perhaps if I was not my consciousness would have ended up somewhere else that was better but who can say. I can say that I wish my parents' other child had been born and that I was not. 



I don't find comfort in thinking my existence is the worse of two options, predictably it fills me with dread. Like there was a cosmic mistake or misdeed when I came to exist as I do now and that it was in some way my fault. Did I take a wrong turn before I could even know it? Should I have died well before now? Would my mom feel better if I did? I don't know, but I suspect those to be true more often than not.

  
I don't want to die, but I do wish I had never existed. I'm not sure I want to change that feeling either so would something like therapy even work?

Aggression.title: Legal Action Advice
Aggression.body:
About three/four weeks ago I went through an incident of sexual harassment/assault at work from a customer. He was black out drunk (I work at a pub) and the way it was handled by my work wasn’t very professional. He was kicked out and told he wasn’t allowed to come back in to pay his tab without talking to my boss or my male coworker first since I made it clear I did not want to have contact with him. 

Well my boss allowed him to come into work yesterday without informing me. And not just to pay his tab, he was allowed to stay and drink. Thankfully I had someone else covering the opening part of my shift but was planning on coming in earlier to help with the bar since there was an event so I knew the restaurant was super busy. I was notified by my male coworker that he showed up so I had to wait till he was gone to come in for my shift. 

One of my regulars is a state trooper and he pulled me aside to tell me that from a professional view, I could take it further if the incident made me this uncomfortable (he wasn’t informed much on what happened). I didn’t have intent to pursue anything legal cause I thought he’d be barred on the days i work, but now I’m not sure what I want to do. 

The statie told me that the guy admits he doesn’t remember what happened but takes full accountability for it and that he wants to apologize to me in person but on my terms. My boss also has talked about him coming in to apologize and I’ve expressed very clearly before that I don’t want to talk to him or hear an “I’m sorry for sexually assaulting you” apology, even if he has owned up to what happened. 

I just wanted to not have him in when I’m working or still be there when I’m into work. He’s been very drunk/overserved numerous times before this incident, and now dealing with that, i don’t want to deal with what could happen if he got blacked out drunk again (if he didn’t remember what he did, he could just as well do it again). But now since he’s just allowed back I’m not sure what legal action I could take if i chose to do that. What would be the options I could take? Cause honestly my biggest option is just quitting my job and working at a different place since it’s not the first sexual harassment incident I’ve gone through and it’s definitely not the last, and it’s clear my boss can’t handle dealing with situations properly.

Discrimination.title: Why does society expectations about having one of each genders mess with us?
Discrimination.body:
I know there are people out there who say they generally don’t care what genders their babies are. I wish I was one of those people. First and foremost, of course I just want happy and healthy children and I know whatever I get I will love them! Yes, we all know that there are people out there who struggle with conceiving or who have a bad experience in having children. I get that! 
We have had a miscarriage in between having our children and it was a hard experience to go through. I feel society constantly makes you feel like having one of each is the ultimate dream. We are always reminded by these expectations! I know I cannot control the gender, but I just wish I didn’t feel I wasn’t missing out on not having a daughter. When I think deeply about why I want a daughter, it’s basically because I get caught up worrying about what other people say about our family or them placing their pity over us for having only boys. I hate the feeling! I love my boys, but wish I had the experience of parenting both genders as well as having my boys. I would not have another one just to try for a girl. I would only have another knowing I am 100% content about having another boy. I feel when my parents or in laws talk about it you can sense their disappointment and it makes me feel sad. Anyone else know what I mean? Can you connect to this post? If so, talk me through how you feel now and how you overcame these annoying feelings.

Mental Health.title: Struggling to feel excited in first trimester
Mental Health.body:
TW: talk of infant death and miscarriage. 

I (f21) am expecting my first baby with my husband (m23). I really want to be happy and excited and hopeful, but ever since I was a little girl and I found out about miscarriage/stillbirth, I’ve had such a deep fear of pregnancy/child loss. 

Lmp date was 4/20/2025, but at our first ultrasound when I should have been almost 9 weeks, baby was measuring at 6w 5d and they found a large (more than 50% the size of the sac) SCH adjacent to the gestational sac. There was no real reason or explanation for either thing and I feel like I was sent home to either miscarry or not until our next appointment on July 17th where I should be 10.5 weeks. Our fetus is confirmed IUP and viable with a good heartbeat. 

I know I should try to hold on to the indescribable joy of hearing our child’s heartbeat for the first time, but seeing the massive pocket of blood directly afterwards and being told we are measuring 2.5 weeks behind has unfortunately overshadowed that beautiful moment and made me feel like I can’t be happy or excited. 

With the lack of information of course fell into a Google search hole and from what I can tell, my risk of pregnancy loss or stillbirth has gone up quite significantly. Everytime the nausea eases up or my boobs feel slightly less sore I’m horrified that my baby is just dead. 

I just don’t know how to be happy or excited when the risk of loss is so great. I keep trying to remind myself that I am pregnant today and that’s all that matters. I’ve greatly increased my vitamin c, d and A Lipaic acid intake within my diet to help the sch heal and reabsorb and so far at 8w 2d I have not had any bleeding or spotting. I’m resting as much as I can and I’ve put myself on pelvic rest to try to help my body and hopefully not bleed. 

Idk. I just feel like I’m doing all I can but I can’t help but feel soooo guilty for how negative I’m feeling. My family keeps saying to just manifest good things and put good vibes out there, so I can’t help but feel like if I do lose the baby it’ll be because of my inability to be happy and hopeful all the time. 

Through all of this, my husband has been my absolute rock and safe space. He has lit up this experience so much and kept me as positive and happy as possible, but he’s on a work trip this week and I’m just here alone with the dogs trying to take care of all of us all while scrutinizing every tiny change in cramping and discharge and just waiting for something awful to happen. I just really don’t want to miscarry while he’s away. I really don’t want to miscarry at all. I understand that in the human experience it is a negative thing to wish to a positive experience, and a positive thing to embrace a negative experience, but how the fuck do I embrace this awful feeling. I feel like I’ll never be able to breathe again, even if the baby ends up being born how am I going to deal with the anxiety of SIDS or car accidents or fucking lightning striking my child. How do moms do this??

Discrimination.title: Why does society expectations about having one of each genders mess with us?
Discrimination.body:
I know there are people out there who say they generally don’t care what genders their babies are. I wish I was one of those people. First and foremost, of course I just want happy and healthy children and I know whatever I get I will love them! Yes, we all know that there are people out there who struggle with conceiving or who have a bad experience in having children. I get that! 
We have had a miscarriage in between having our children and it was a hard experience to go through. I feel society constantly makes you feel like having one of each is the ultimate dream. We are always reminded by these expectations! I know I cannot control the gender, but I just wish I didn’t feel I wasn’t missing out on not having a daughter. When I think deeply about why I want a daughter, it’s basically because I get caught up worrying about what other people say about our family or them placing their pity over us for having only boys. I hate the feeling! I love my boys, but wish I had the experience of parenting both genders as well as having my boys. I would not have another one just to try for a girl. I would only have another knowing I am 100% content about having another boy. I feel when my parents or in laws talk about it you can sense their disappointment and it makes me feel sad. Anyone else know what I mean? Can you connect to this post? If so, talk me through how you feel now and how you overcame these annoying feelings.

Abuse.title: Always Worried I Was Not Meant To Be Born
Abuse.body:
Before I was born my parents had gone through two other pregnancies. One of them resulted in my sister, the other tragically ended in a late miscarriage. I was conceived of about a year later and I am nearly certain I was a consolation child for my mother. I do not think my dad wanted me and I think my mom has a deep disappointment over well, me. 



I don't say this without reason. The first thing that comes to mind is that my dad has always hated me and I do mean always. For example my earliest memory of him is a mocking monologue of how I described a television show, the disgust was dripping from his tone. My mom seemed more subtly disgusted by me but it was certainly there. The overcompensated declarations of affection, the perceivable lack of joy in her eyes when around me, and the inverse with my sister all point to that being the case. There's much more I could add but it would be pedantic. I'm confident in how I have judged the situation, but confidence means little when I feel terrible about the whole thing.

  
There's no resentment for how my family feels about me in my heart, but there is a hole where something is missing. The root of that I can only imagine is that the strands of fate simply never intended for it to be filled. Point being I don't think I should have been born nor that I was meant to be born. Perhaps if I was not my consciousness would have ended up somewhere else that was better but who can say. I can say that I wish my parents' other child had been born and that I was not. 



I don't find comfort in thinking my existence is the worse of two options, predictably it fills me with dread. Like there was a cosmic mistake or misdeed when I came to exist as I do now and that it was in some way my fault. Did I take a wrong turn before I could even know it? Should I have died well before now? Would my mom feel better if I did? I don't know, but I suspect those to be true more often than not.

  
I don't want to die, but I do wish I had never existed. I'm not sure I want to change that feeling either so would something like therapy even work?

Medical.title: Haven’t Had a Period Since My Suction Abortion – Was the June 3 Spotting My Period?
Medical.body:
Hi everyone,

I had a suction abortion (manual vacuum aspiration) on **April 19th, 2025**. I was just **1 month and 1 week pregnant** at the time. I’m now over 9 weeks post-procedure, and I still haven’t had a full period, so I’m hoping to get some thoughts or shared experiences.

Here’s what’s happened:

* **Post-abortion:** I recovered normally with no pain or heavy bleeding.
* On **May 21–22,** I had intense lower abdominal cramps, but they went away after two days.
* On **June 3**, I saw some red blood on the tissue paper while wiping after urinating. It looked like a small amount of fresh blood — similar to what I might see on day 3–4 of a typical period — but it only lasted half a day. I wore a pad, but there was no blood on it at all. Little cramps but no breast tenderness or PMS-like symptoms.
* On **June 19**, I had another episode of strong cramping and pulsating pain in the lower abdomen, along with intense pain in the pelvic region during bowel movements. I went to the clinic the next day, where they performed all the necessary tests and an ultrasound, and said everything looked normal.

As of today (**June 24**), I still haven’t had a proper period. I’m not on any birth control, and I don’t have a history of irregular periods or PCOS. I do have subclinical hypothyroidism, and I tested positive for **thyroid peroxidase antibodies** earlier this year **(TPO 60)**, but my thyroid levels were said to be in the normal range recently **(TSH 2.35).**

My main questions are:

* Was the June 3rd spotting likely my first period, or just hormonal spotting?
* Is it normal to still not have a period more than 9 weeks after a suction abortion?

Would really appreciate any insight, especially from people who had delayed periods after surgical abortion. Thanks so much.

Mental Health.title: Struggling to feel excited in first trimester
Mental Health.body:
TW: talk of infant death and miscarriage. 

I (f21) am expecting my first baby with my husband (m23). I really want to be happy and excited and hopeful, but ever since I was a little girl and I found out about miscarriage/stillbirth, I’ve had such a deep fear of pregnancy/child loss. 

Lmp date was 4/20/2025, but at our first ultrasound when I should have been almost 9 weeks, baby was measuring at 6w 5d and they found a large (more than 50% the size of the sac) SCH adjacent to the gestational sac. There was no real reason or explanation for either thing and I feel like I was sent home to either miscarry or not until our next appointment on July 17th where I should be 10.5 weeks. Our fetus is confirmed IUP and viable with a good heartbeat. 

I know I should try to hold on to the indescribable joy of hearing our child’s heartbeat for the first time, but seeing the massive pocket of blood directly afterwards and being told we are measuring 2.5 weeks behind has unfortunately overshadowed that beautiful moment and made me feel like I can’t be happy or excited. 

With the lack of information of course fell into a Google search hole and from what I can tell, my risk of pregnancy loss or stillbirth has gone up quite significantly. Everytime the nausea eases up or my boobs feel slightly less sore I’m horrified that my baby is just dead. 

I just don’t know how to be happy or excited when the risk of loss is so great. I keep trying to remind myself that I am pregnant today and that’s all that matters. I’ve greatly increased my vitamin c, d and A Lipaic acid intake within my diet to help the sch heal and reabsorb and so far at 8w 2d I have not had any bleeding or spotting. I’m resting as much as I can and I’ve put myself on pelvic rest to try to help my body and hopefully not bleed. 

Idk. I just feel like I’m doing all I can but I can’t help but feel soooo guilty for how negative I’m feeling. My family keeps saying to just manifest good things and put good vibes out there, so I can’t help but feel like if I do lose the baby it’ll be because of my inability to be happy and hopeful all the time. 

Through all of this, my husband has been my absolute rock and safe space. He has lit up this experience so much and kept me as positive and happy as possible, but he’s on a work trip this week and I’m just here alone with the dogs trying to take care of all of us all while scrutinizing every tiny change in cramping and discharge and just waiting for something awful to happen. I just really don’t want to miscarry while he’s away. I really don’t want to miscarry at all. I understand that in the human experience it is a negative thing to wish to a positive experience, and a positive thing to embrace a negative experience, but how the fuck do I embrace this awful feeling. I feel like I’ll never be able to breathe again, even if the baby ends up being born how am I going to deal with the anxiety of SIDS or car accidents or fucking lightning striking my child. How do moms do this??

I keep wondering if I’m a horrible person for not wanting to go through with this pregnancy, but deep down I know I’m trying to make the best decision for everyone involved including the child I already have.

If anyone has been through something like this or has experience with later abortion, I’d really appreciate any advice, support, or just to hear that I’m not alone.

Thank you for reading.

Discrimination.title: Why does society expectations about having one of each genders mess with us?
Discrimination.body:
I know there are people out there who say they generally don’t care what genders their babies are. I wish I was one of those people. First and foremost, of course I just want happy and healthy children and I know whatever I get I will love them! Yes, we all know that there are people out there who struggle with conceiving or who have a bad experience in having children. I get that! 
We have had a miscarriage in between having our children and it was a hard experience to go through. I feel society constantly makes you feel like having one of each is the ultimate dream. We are always reminded by these expectations! I know I cannot control the gender, but I just wish I didn’t feel I wasn’t missing out on not having a daughter. When I think deeply about why I want a daughter, it’s basically because I get caught up worrying about what other people say about our family or them placing their pity over us for having only boys. I hate the feeling! I love my boys, but wish I had the experience of parenting both genders as well as having my boys. I would not have another one just to try for a girl. I would only have another knowing I am 100% content about having another boy. I feel when my parents or in laws talk about it you can sense their disappointment and it makes me feel sad. Anyone else know what I mean? Can you connect to this post? If so, talk me through how you feel now and how you overcame these annoying feelings.

title: MA at home, a lot easier than expected so i’m not sure it worked?

Aggression.title: Legal Action Advice
Aggression.body:
About three/four weeks ago I went through an incident of sexual harassment/assault at work from a customer. He was black out drunk (I work at a pub) and the way it was handled by my work wasn’t very professional. He was kicked out and told he wasn’t allowed to come back in to pay his tab without talking to my boss or my male coworker first since I made it clear I did not want to have contact with him.

We’ve been trying for almost two years with only a miscarriage to show for it. This month lh didn’t spike nearly as high as normal so I felt pretty sure it wasn’t going to be our time this month. Well I just took a test and got a positive. Probably only like 10-12 dpo, but it was definitely positive. 

So now I’m panicked because I did a bunch of things that probably weren’t great. I got a tooth infection and took ibuprofen like candy for 5 days. I did at least let the doctor know that we were ttc so he prescribed pregnancy safe antibiotics just in case. I also couldn’t eat anything but mushy foods for almost a week. So my diet has been terrible. And I quit taking my metformin (prescribed for PCOS) while on the antibiotics because it had terrible gastrointestinal side effects. 

So now I’m feeling guilty as crap and like I might have just ruined our second chance. I’m obviously calling my ob in the morning to get a blood test and discuss these things ASAP. But is this all as bad as I’m thinking it is? Give it to me straight.

Mental Health.title: Struggling to feel excited in first trimester
Mental Health.body:
TW: talk of infant death and miscarriage. 

I (f21) am expecting my first baby with my husband (m23). I really want to be happy and excited and hopeful, but ever since I was a little girl and I found out about miscarriage/stillbirth, I’ve had such a deep fear of pregnancy/child loss. 

Lmp date was 4/20/2025, but at our first ultrasound when I should have been almost 9 weeks, baby was measuring at 6w 5d and they found a large (more than 50% the size of the sac) SCH adjacent to the gestational sac. There was no real reason or explanation for either thing and I feel like I was sent home to either miscarry or not until our next appointment on July 17th where I should be 10.5 weeks. Our fetus is confirmed IUP and viable with a good heartbeat. 

I know I should try to hold on to the indescribable joy of hearing our child’s heartbeat for the first time, but seeing the massive pocket of blood directly afterwards and being told we are measuring 2.5 weeks behind has unfortunately overshadowed that beautiful moment and made me feel like I can’t be happy or excited. 

With the lack of information of course fell into a Google search hole and from what I can tell, my risk of pregnancy loss or stillbirth has gone up quite significantly. Everytime the nausea eases up or my boobs feel slightly less sore I’m horrified that my baby is just dead. 

I just don’t know how to be happy or excited when the risk of loss is so great. I keep trying to remind myself that I am pregnant today and that’s all that matters. I’ve greatly increased my vitamin c, d and A Lipaic acid intake within my diet to help the sch heal and reabsorb and so far at 8w 2d I have not had any bleeding or spotting. I’m resting as much as I can and I’ve put myself on pelvic rest to try to help my body and hopefully not bleed. 

Idk. I just feel like I’m doing all I can but I can’t help but feel soooo guilty for how negative I’m feeling. My family keeps saying to just manifest good things and put good vibes out there, so I can’t help but feel like if I do lose the baby it’ll be because of my inability to be happy and hopeful all the time. 

Through all of this, my husband has been my absolute rock and safe space. He has lit up this experience so much and kept me as positive and happy as possible, but he’s on a work trip this week and I’m just here alone with the dogs trying to take care of all of us all while scrutinizing every tiny change in cramping and discharge and just waiting for something awful to happen. I just really don’t want to miscarry while he’s away. I really don’t want to miscarry at all. I understand that in the human experience it is a negative thing to wish to a positive experience, and a positive thing to embrace a negative experience, but how the fuck do I embrace this awful feeling. I feel like I’ll never be able to breathe again, even if the baby ends up being born how am I going to deal with the anxiety of SIDS or car accidents or fucking lightning striking my child. How do moms do this??

Discrimination.title: Why does society expectations about having one of each genders mess with us?
Discrimination.body:
I know there are people out there who say they generally don’t care what genders their babies are. I wish I was one of those people. First and foremost, of course I just want happy and healthy children and I know whatever I get I will love them! Yes, we all know that there are people out there who struggle with conceiving or who have a bad experience in having children. I get that! 
We have had a miscarriage in between having our children and it was a hard experience to go through. I feel society constantly makes you feel like having one of each is the ultimate dream. We are always reminded by these expectations! I know I cannot control the gender, but I just wish I didn’t feel I wasn’t missing out on not having a daughter. When I think deeply about why I want a daughter, it’s basically because I get caught up worrying about what other people say about our family or them placing their pity over us for having only boys. I hate the feeling! I love my boys, but wish I had the experience of parenting both genders as well as having my boys. I would not have another one just to try for a girl. I would only have another knowing I am 100% content about having another boy. I feel when my parents or in laws talk about it you can sense their disappointment and it makes me feel sad. Anyone else know what I mean? Can you connect to this post? If so, talk me through how you feel now and how you overcame these annoying feelings.

About three/four weeks ago I went through an incident of sexual harassment/assault at work from a customer. He was black out drunk (I work at a pub) and the way it was handled by my work wasn’t very professional. He was kicked out and told he wasn’t allowed to come back in to pay his tab without talking to my boss or my male coworker first since I made it clear I did not want to have contact with him.

I just wanted to not have him in when I’m working or still be there when I’m into work. Medical.title: Recommendations/ Advice for Bisalp?
Medical.body:
As of posting this I reside in the Southern U.S. (TX), and with abortion being practically banned here (there was a woman arrested and placed in jail for 5 months because she had a miscarriage), along with other health concerns (hypothyroidism since childhood, as well as the genetic risk of lupus flairs after pregnancy), as well as my personal ambitions that leave little room for children, I've decided that as soon as I legally and financially can (still under 18 currently), I want to pursue getting a bisalp. (I also have an acute fear of pregnancy and its effects, but that's a minor factor in comparison to other variables). From a practicality perspective it seems to be the most logical since from what I've read it has a high efficacy rate, has few complications, relative cost efficiency, a quick recovery, and leaves open the option for IVF in the improbable case that I decide I do desire biological children later in life. All this being said, although it will likely be several years before I can properly execute my plans, I'd like to collect as much input/ advice as possible so that I can create the most full proof and systematic design to achieve my goal.

I am unlikely to receive any parental financial support and it will be classified as an elective surgery, and although I am not aware of what my financial situation will be in the future, I anticipate that I may not qualify for aid. Unfortunately I reside in a strange middle-class economic range that does not receive welfare but does not have the abundance to pay completely out of pocket. Regardless, I plan to prepare for the worst possible case and save to pay for the entirety of the cost myself. Due to the high medical costs in the U.S., and the general lack of autonomy women are provided in the medical world, I am seriously considering medical tourism, perhaps Turkey, Austria, Thailand, or Slovakia, as I have heard generally positive things about procedures performed in those countries.

I appreciate any advice, experiences, and perspectives, but would kindly ask that anymore providing input would abstain from attempting to dissuade me or change my decision. I am well aware of the consequences and risks of my actions and have given extensive thought to this particular topic. I realize that I am young, but please do not mistake my youth for naivety or immaturity.
